title: Is AI Safe to Try?
hook: Yes — using a mainstream chatbot won't break your computer or hurt you. The real risks are mundane: oversharing personal data and believing something that isn't true.
key_points: A chatbot can't damage your device or 'escape' — it just generates text.
The genuine risks are privacy (what you share) and accuracy (what you believe).
Stick to well-known apps; ignore sketchy 'free AI' sites and pop-ups.
You're in control: you can stop, delete chats, and share nothing sensitive.
content_html: A lot of people hesitate to try AI because it feels vaguely dangerous, as if a chatbot might do something to their computer or take on a life of its own. It won't. A mainstream chatbot is just a website or app that generates text in response to what you type. It can't infect your device, can't access your files unless you deliberately upload them, and certainly can't "escape." Using one is about as risky to your machine as reading a web page.
extra_html: That doesn't mean there's nothing to be thoughtful about — just that the real risks are ordinary, not science-fiction. The first is privacy: what you type may be stored and used to improve the model, so don't paste in passwords, ID numbers, or sensitive personal details. The second is accuracy: the AI can state false things confidently, so don't act on important information without checking it. A third, smaller one is sketchy imitators — there are shady "free AI" sites and app-store knockoffs designed to harvest data or push scams, so stick to the well-known names. Beyond that, you're firmly in control: you can close the tab, delete your conversation history, and choose to share nothing personal. Try it the way you'd try any new app — a little cautiously at first, then freely once you see how it behaves.

related.title: Your First Hour with AI
related.hook: Forget the hype and the fear. Open a free chatbot, type a real question in plain English, and have a conversation. That's the whole on-ramp — you already know how.

related.title: Your Data & Privacy
related.hook: When you type into a free AI tool, you might be the product. What you share can be stored, reviewed by humans, and used to train future models — so share like it's not private.

related.title: When AI Makes Things Up
related.hook: AI 'hallucinations' aren't glitches — they're the technology working as designed. A model that always predicts a plausible next word will sometimes produce a plausible falsehood.

flashcards.prompt: What are the real risks of trying a mainstream AI chatbot?

choices.text: Oversharing personal data and trusting inaccurate answers
It could infect or damage your computer
It might physically escape and act on its own

flashcards.explanation_html: A chatbot just produces text — it can't harm your device. The genuine cautions are privacy (what you type) and accuracy (what you believe).

flashcards.prompt: How can you keep your first AI experiences safe?
flashcards.back_html: Use well-known apps (skip sketchy 'free AI' sites), share nothing sensitive, and verify anything important. You can stop or delete your chats anytime.
